transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-01-15
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Recorded at: 2028-01-15T15:30:00Z
Attendees: Ethan Cole (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Marcus Li (Ironshore Head of ML), Anika Shah (CTO), Roberto Gomez (Procurement)

Summary:
Quick renewal/extension check-in focused on bridging current commitment through Q2 while Ironshore onboards South Asia region. Discussion covered capacity uplift sizing, latency SLOs, private VPC options vs hosted, SOC 2/KMS concerns, and an agreement to run benchmarks before contract amendment. Next steps and owners captured.

Topics:
- Commitment bridge vs full renewal
- South Asia region onramp (Singapore and Mumbai clusters)
- Latency vs cost tradeoffs, batching and KV cache settings
- Security: SSO/SAML, KMS, audit logs, SOC 2 evidence
- Procurement timeline and PO requirements

Action items (recap included in body): see metadata action_items

Transcript body:
[00:00] Ethan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, really appreciate you squeezing this in. Ethan Cole from Redwood, with Priya, our SE. How's it going Marcus?
[00:12] Marcus: Hey Ethan, good, busy week. We wanted to make sure we had a quick sync. Anika is here to talk timing and Roberto for procurement.
[00:22] Anika: Hi all. Short on time but want to get clear on the bridging option — we don't want an 8-week gap while we stand up South Asia.
[00:35] Ethan: Totally, that's the call. We recommended a bridging amendment vs full contract roll today, that keeps your current rates and adds a region add-on for South Asia when ready.
[00:47] Priya: Quick technical note — for South Asia we typically recommend the mid-tier quantized variants and a dedicated pool for steady QPS. That gives better predictability on latency at a lower cost, especially if you tune KV cache.
[01:05] Marcus: Quick question, when you say "KV cache"—is that the same approach as your hosted prefix cache? We saw different behavior earlier in tests.
[01:18] Priya: Yeah, sorry - KV cache (sometimes transcribed as KV cash in earlier notes) is the key-value attention cache. On our runtime it's configurable; we can pin warm caches on the dedicated nodes to reduce cold-start tps. The prefix caching behavior differs by model and sequence length.
[01:40] Marcus: Ok, makes sense. Our peak QPS right now is about 600 rps spiking to 1.2k in the US east region, and around 120 rps in EU, almost zero in APAC. We'll share exact numbers after.
[01:56] Ethan: That's perfect. For sizing the South Asia cluster we need those numbers plus an estimate for the first 90 days. If it's low to start we can provision burst capacity instead of fully reserved capacity.
[02:10] Anika: Our main constraint is 99th latency under 450 ms for user-facing flows, and we can't exceed a 25% cost increase in total infra spend for this quarter.
[02:22] Ethan: Understood — so SLO and budget guardrails. That's where the batching + quantization discussion comes back. We can illustrate cost/latency curves for the three model variants we recommended.
[02:36] Roberto: From procurement, timeline wise we need a final amended contract by Feb 1 to process PO by Feb 10. Any delays push to next quarter. Also we have a few standard redlines around data residency and audit controls.
[02:50] Ethan: We'll prioritize that. We'll also include SOC 2 artifacts and our KMS integration notes. Priya, can you confirm the keys/HSM story for private deployments?
[02:59] Priya: Yep — in Private (V P C) mode we support customer-managed KMS and HSM-backed keys for token encryption and audit logs. For Hosted we offer envelope encryption with Redwood-managed KMS but can integrate with external KMS via a key-wrapping flow. We'll put the doc links in the follow up.
[03:20] Marcus: Any material difference in egress or bandwidth costs between dedicated and private? Our network team will flag anything with high egress.
[03:28] Priya: Egress is cloud dependent — if you're on Dedicated in our managed VPC you'll see standard cloud provider egress. On Private on-prem or a colocated setup it depends on your peering. We can provide a sample bill calc.
[03:40] Anika: Also, do you have an SLA uplift for reserved pools? Right now our pain is variable latency during spikes.
[03:48] Ethan: Reserved capacity gives a latency SLO window — we can commit to 99th latency targets for a given commit level. If you need hard SLOs for spikes, we recommend a hybrid: base reserved plus burstable capacity. That avoids overcommit spend.
[04:04] Marcus: I want to understand the fallback behavior if a region is unhealthy. Do requests route to other regions automatically and how does that affect latency?
[04:13] Priya: We support smart routing with policy-based fallback. You can prefer low-latency region but fall back to cheaper region or to a smaller model variant. We'll include routing policy samples in the playbook. Note: cross-region fallbacks add network latency obviously.
[04:30] Ethan: For the bridging amend specifically, the legal team suggested a clause: 'commitment bridge' that extends the current rate for 90 days with an option to convert to a multi-region commit. That gives procurement breathing room.
[04:44] Roberto: That sounds workable; need to review contract language. Also add pricing for volume buckets and for the South Asia onramp as a line item.
[04:55] Ethan: Will do. We'll add a column in the pricing spreadsheet for South Asia - two SKUs: Singapore (sg) and Mumbai (bom) with burst and reserved options.
[05:07] Marcus: About benchmarks — can we do a controlled run with our model artifact? We use a custom fine-tuned open model with 3B parameters.
[05:16] Priya: Yes, we can run your artifact in a staging dedicated pool. We'll need the model files and a small prompt set. We'll do a throughput/latency bench and an eval for output parity vs your current infra. Note that quantization may slightly change outputs; we'll surface delta metrics.
[05:35] Marcus: Ok we'll provide model + prompts. Also need to know how long that benchmark takes.
[05:40] Priya: Typically 2-3 days to provision and run, then 1-2 days to analyze results. We can target the week of Jan 22.
[05:51] Anika: Any gating security docs we need before benchmarks? We won't upload PII.
[05:56] Ethan: No PII required. We'll still provide an NDA-friendly data handling note and a readme on how we isolate test artifacts.
[06:06] Roberto: Procurement also wants to include a clause about audit logs retention — we need 7 years for certain logs, is that possible?
[06:15] Priya: 7 years is longer than our default retention; enterprise add-on for extended logs is possible. We'll include options and costs.
[06:25] Marcus: Back to cost, can you show us a sample cost for 1k baseline QPS in US + 200 QPS in EU + 200 QPS in SG with 50% cache hit? We need to compare to our cloud-hosted transformer infra.
[06:40] Ethan: We'll do that. We'll produce a TCO calc with a few kernel points — current vs dedicated vs private. Expect some variance but we'll give a clear delta per 1M tokens.
[06:52] Anika: About SSO and role-based access — we require SAML and SCIM for user provisioning.
[06:59] Priya: Redwood supports SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning, and RBAC with custom roles. We'll attach the SSO setup doc.
[07:08] Marcus: Any outages in last 6 months we should be aware of? We need stability metrics for procurement.
[07:15] Ethan: We'll include a recent incident summary and uptime numbers. Our SLA history shows >99.95% for dedicated customers; we'll include the incident postmortems sanitized.
[07:27] Roberto: On invoicing, we prefer monthly invoices with PO net30. Can Redwood accommodate?
[07:33] Ethan: Yes, monthly invoicing net30 is standard for enterprise customers. We'll add that to the amendment.
[07:40] Marcus: If the benchmark shows latency drift with quantization, is rollback to float easy?
[07:46] Priya: Yes, rollbacks are supported. The runtime supports multiple model variants side-by-side and automated rollback on quality regression. We'll show a canary rollout plan. Sometimes the token cost tradeoff matters.
[07:58] Ethan: Great — sounds like plan of attack: 1) you send model + prompts (Marcus), 2) we run bench (Priya), 3) we draft amendment + pricing (Ethan), 4) procurement confirms timeline (Roberto).
[08:12] Anika: One more ask — can you include a gating clause that requires a successful bench to trigger the South Asia reserved capacity?
[08:21] Ethan: Yes that's reasonable; we can make the South Asia conversion conditional on benchmarks meeting agreed SLOs. We'll craft that language.
[08:31] Marcus: I'll share the exact traffic export and the sample prompt set today.
[08:36] Roberto: I'll email procurement redlines by Friday.
[08:40] Ethan: Perfect. We'll follow up with the pricing spreadsheet and the security packet.
[08:46] Priya: I'll schedule the bench and provision a staging pool. Expect calendar invite and access details.
[08:52] Ethan: Any other blockers?
[08:55] Anika: No blockers, just alignment on the PO timeline.
[08:59] Ethan: Ok, we'll shoot for amendment draft 2028-01-20 and bench week of 2028-01-22.
[09:07] Marcus: Thanks everyone.
[09:10] Ethan: Thanks, talk soon.

Note: timestamps above are rough markers; actual call ran ~55 minutes with deeper sub-discussion on billing tiers, test harness details and legal redlines.
